title: Subtree Fundamentals
description: Use git subtree to merge external repositories into your project without submodule complexity.

data.text: git subtree allows you to merge another repository into a subdirectory of your repository while preserving the external repository's history. Unlike submodules, subtrees do not require special Git commands for everyday use — the external code lives directly in your repository.

git subtree add clones the external repository and merges it into a subdirectory of your project. The --prefix flag specifies the target subdirectory, and --squash optionally collapses the entire external history into a single commit.

data.title: Add a subtree to your project
data.code:
# Add a subtree with full history
git subtree add --prefix=external/lib \
  https://github.com/example/lib.git \
  main --squash

# Output:
# Added directory 'external/lib'

# Without --squash (preserves full external history):
git subtree add --prefix=external/lib \
  https://github.com/example/lib.git \
  main

data.text: When the external repository has new commits, use git subtree pull to merge those changes into your subtree. This fetches the external repository and merges new commits into your prefix directory.

data.title: Pull updates from a subtree
data.code:
# Pull latest changes from the subtree remote
git subtree pull --prefix=external/lib \
  https://github.com/example/lib.git \
  main --squash

# Output:
#   * new subtree commit
# From https://github.com/example/lib.git
#  * branch            main       -> FETCH_HEAD

# Resolve any conflicts, then commit

data.text: Pushing changes back to the subtree
If you modify files inside a subtree and want to push those changes back to the external repository, use git subtree push. This extracts the subtree commits and pushes them to a branch on the remote.

data.title: Push subtree changes back to the remote
data.code:
# Push changes from the subtree back to the remote
git subtree push --prefix=external/lib \
  https://github.com/example/lib.git \
  my-feature-branch

# This extracts the commits that affect external/lib
# and pushes them to the my-feature-branch branch
# on the external/lib repository

data.text: git subtree split extracts the commits that affect a specific subtree directory and creates a new branch containing only those commits. This is useful for pushing changes back to the upstream repository or for creating a clean history of the subtree.

data.title: Split a subtree into a new branch
data.code:
# Extract commits affecting external/lib into a new branch
git subtree split --prefix=external/lib \
  -b lib-split-branch

# The new branch contains only the commits
# that modified files inside external/lib

# Push the split branch to the upstream repository
git push https://github.com/example/lib.git \
  lib-split-branch:main

items: **Simple teams**: Subtrees are easier for developers who do not know Git well
**No special commands**: Developers clone and pull normally; the external code is just files
**Vendored dependencies**: Embed libraries you need to customize occasionally
**Single repository**: Avoid the overhead of managing multiple repositories

data.title: Subtrees increase repository size
data.text: Because subtrees embed the external repository's code directly in your repository, your repository grows with each subtree addition. For large external dependencies, subtrees can significantly increase clone times and repository size.

items.question: Does Git have subtree built in?
items.answer: git subtree is not built into core Git. It is a separate script that is included in the Git contrib directory. Install it separately on Windows or use the Git for Windows installer which includes contrib scripts.

items.question: Can I use subtrees with GitHub?
items.answer: Yes. Subtrees work with any Git remote, including GitHub. Because the external code lives in your repository, GitHub shows it as normal code.

items.question: What if I need to update the subtree URL?
items.answer: There is no direct command to update the subtree URL. You must remove the subtree and re-add it with the new URL, or manually update the .gitmodules file if you use a wrapper.

items.question: Can I have multiple subtrees in one repository?
items.answer: Yes. Use a different --prefix for each subtree. Each subtree maintains its own independent history.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git subtree merges external repositories into a subdirectory
--prefix specifies the target subdirectory; --squash compresses history
git subtree pull fetches and merges upstream changes
git subtree push sends local subtree changes back upstream
Subtrees are simpler than submodules but increase repository size
